docRequirement: code-review.md:316 binds a re-report to carry per-finding state: "When Claude fixes reported findings later in the session, it reports them again, and Claude Code marks each finding in the new list as fixed, skipped, or no change needed." The second `ReportFindings` call must therefore be distinguishable from the first at the level of the individual finding, with exactly three states — `fixed`, `skipped`, `no change needed`. The same page (:312) fixes the rest of the entry shape and is already satisfied: "Each entry shows the file location, a one-sentence summary, and a category tag such as `correctness` when the finding carries one."
current: `FindingSchema` (packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:269-276) is exactly `{file, summary, failureScenario, category?}` — no state field of any kind. `ReportFindingsSchema` (:278-281) wraps it as `{findings: array(1..100)}` and nothing else, so a call carries no top-level report state either. The absence is enforced twice: the projected model schema closes the finding object — probed live, `getToolDefsAsJsonSchema({prefix:'mcp__session__',projection:'pi'})` emits the finding item with `"additionalProperties": false` and `required:[file,summary,failureScenario]` (only the TOP-level `additionalProperties` is deleted, tool-defs.ts:1373), so the model is affirmatively told no such field exists; and zod 4 `z.object` strips anyway — probed, `ReportFindingsSchema.safeParse({findings:[{file,summary,failureScenario,outcome:'fixed'}]})` returns `ok:true` with `outcome` gone, no error. The handler re-projects only the four fields (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/report-findings.ts:63-68) onto `structuredContent: {findings}` (:76), and its text fallback `renderFinding` (:40-47) prints only location, summary and "Fails when:", so a second report is byte-identical in shape to the first on both surfaces. The tool description never asks for a re-report: TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS.ReportFindings (tool-defs.ts:621-626) says only "Call this when active code-review instructions tell you to report findings" and its last line is about one-call completeness, not about reporting again after fixing. The schema's own doc-comment (:262-268) cites `tools-reference.md:45` alone and asserts "No field of theirs is renamed and none is added" — tools-reference.md:45 is indeed the whole basis, and re-fetched today it still never mentions the re-report (grep for `outcome`/`skipped`/`no change needed` over the 465-line page: no hit on ReportFindings). The tool is shipped and reachable (SESSION_TOOL_DEFS entry tool-defs.ts:1048; granted implicitly to read-only review agents by SUBAGENT_ALWAYS_AVAILABLE_TOOLS in packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:83; bound as `mcp__session__ReportFindings` at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-tool-descriptor.ts:327 and aliased at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:81), so this is a narrow schema gap in a live tool, not dead code.
divergence: One optional field is missing from `FindingSchema`, and with it the three documented values. This is not a key-name mismatch — there is no key to rename: `grep -a` for `no_change_needed`/`noChangeNeeded`/`no change needed` over packages+apps (excluding dist) returns zero hits, and the only `outcome` identifiers in session-tools-core are the sibling task-tool subsystem and a local helper at handlers/push-notification.ts:79. Two halves, both needed: (1) the payload cannot express the state, and because the projected item schema is `additionalProperties:false` we also advertise that it cannot; (2) nothing tells the model to report again after fixing, so even with the field added the second call would never happen. Everything else code-review.md binds about a findings entry (file location, one-sentence summary, `category` tag) is already correct, including the documented placement of `category` next to the location.

change.what: Add one optional field: `outcome: z.enum(['fixed', 'skipped', 'no_change_needed']).optional().describe('Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding.')`. Optional is required, not a convenience — a first report must stay schema-identical, and the doc scopes the state to the re-report. Keep `z.object` (not `.strict()`); the enum is what rejects a bad value. The three value spellings: the page writes them in prose ("fixed, skipped, or no change needed"), so `no_change_needed` is the snake_case form, matching Claude's live ReportFindings tool definition, which carries `outcome` with exactly that enum and the description "Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding". Update the doc comment in the same edit: it currently cites `tools-reference.md:45` alone and states "No field of theirs is renamed and none is added" — that sentence is now false, and the new citation is `code-review.md:316`, which is where this requirement lives and the reason the tools-reference-derived schema lacked it.

One added line, before the final "Report every finding in one call" line: when re-reporting findings after fixing them (only if the active instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened — `fixed`, `skipped`, or `no_change_needed`. Without this the field is unreachable in practice: nothing else in the product supplies re-report instructions (no `/code-review` skill ships; `apps/electron/resources/skills/` holds only `plugin-creator` and `skill-creator`). Does not move the pinned schema digest — the digest is over `inputSchema` only.

change.symbol: ReportedFinding (:28-33), the re-projection in handleReportFindings (:63-68), renderFinding (:40-47)
change.what: Add `outcome?: 'fixed' | 'skipped' | 'no_change_needed'` to `ReportedFinding`; pass it through the re-projection with the same conditional spread `category` uses (`...(finding.outcome === undefined ? {} : { outcome: finding.outcome })`) so an absent outcome does not grow an empty key — the existing test at report-findings.test.ts:42 pins exactly that property for `category`. Render it in the text too, not only on `structuredContent`: nothing in this fork reads `structuredContent` (grep -a over apps/electron/src, packages/ui/src, apps/webui, apps/viewer, apps/cli: zero hits), so the text fallback is the only surface a state can reach today, and the file's own precedent is that `category` rides the rendered location line. A one-token suffix on the numbered line (e.g. `1. path/to/file.ts [correctness] — fixed`) is enough; do not fold it into the summary.

Two cases, per the minimum-non-duplicative rule. Positive: a re-report whose findings carry `outcome` round-trips onto `structuredContent.findings` AND appears in `content[0].text`, while a finding without `outcome` does not grow the key (`Object.hasOwn(...,'outcome') === false`). Negative/boundary: `outcome: 'done'` (or any non-enum value) fails the WHOLE call with `findings.0.outcome` in the error text — the existing whole-call-failure invariant at :45-56 must extend to the new field rather than degrade to a silent strip, which is the current behaviour and the defect.

Recompute the three digest strings — `schemaIdentity`, `modelSchemaVersion`, `bindingSchemaVersion` all embed the same sha256 (currently `f867a527…9c9f6a`) over `canonicalJson(definition.inputSchema)` (pi-harness-baseline.test.ts:96-108, payload passed at :146-152). `handlerSchemaVersion` is a static source-path string and must NOT change. The test 'pins deterministic production schema contracts for every effective tool' (:512-521) asserts `tools.schemaContracts` equals the live map exactly, so it fails until this row is regenerated; nothing else in the fixture moves, since the description is not part of the digested payload.

blastRadius: Contained to session-tools-core plus one pinned fixture, but it does cross a wire boundary. Registry: `SESSION_TOOL_DEFS` (tool-defs.ts:1048); the schema is a public export (packages/session-tools-core/src/index.ts:280) and the handler and `ReportedFinding` type too (handlers/index.ts:65-66) — no consumer outside the package reads either today (grep -a for `ReportedFinding`: only the handler, its test and the barrel). Wire: `structuredContent` travels from the Pi subprocess to the renderer as `tool_result.structuredContent?: Record<string, unknown>` (packages/core/src/types/message.ts:973), packed at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:5529, unpacked at packages/shared/src/agent/backend/pi/event-adapter.ts:101-116 and emitted at :784-818, and relayed for the cloud backend at packages/shared/src/agent/backend/nestor-cloud/tool-executor.ts:260-288. The type is an open `Record`, so a new key needs no wire-schema edit — but it is a cross-process payload change, which is a risk trigger in this repo, so the affected-boundary check is the harness-contract suite plus the pi event-adapter tests, not just the handler test. Contract test that WILL fail until regenerated: packages/pi-agent-server/src/__tests__/harness-contract/pi-harness-baseline.test.ts:512-521. Availability paths that carry the field unchanged: runtime-agent-definitions.ts:83, runtime-agent-definition.ts:81, harness-tool-descriptor.ts:199 and :327. No persistence boundary — findings are not stored anywhere; no i18n key; no permission change (`safeMode: 'allow'`, `readOnly: true` stay correct, the tool still only shapes its own result). SIBLING SUBSYSTEM DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED: the in-product review path is Pi's own `review` tool (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/review-tool.ts:254-350), whose findings contract is `REVIEW_FINDINGS_SCHEMA` (packages/shared/src/prompts/review.ts:59-114: `{title, body, priority, confidence, file, line}` + `verdict` + `explanation`) — a different shape, a one-shot inline result, and it never calls `ReportFindings`; its fixture digest is `source-state-schema` over the factory source, so editing `FindingSchema` does not move it. Finally, the schema is embedded in two UNTRACKED build outputs, apps/electron/resources/session-mcp-server/index.js and apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js, which `electron:dev` serves — the change is invisible in a running dev app until those are rebuilt.
userImpact: None observable today. Two independent reasons, both verified: nothing renders a findings list at all (no file under apps/electron/src, packages/ui/src, apps/webui, apps/viewer or apps/cli reads `structuredContent`), and nothing in the product ever asks for a re-report — no `/code-review` command or skill ships, and the one review flow users can reach, the Pi `review` tool, returns its own separate one-shot payload and never calls `ReportFindings`. Two things would surface it. (1) An imported Claude plugin whose code-review skill supplies exactly the documented re-report instructions: a Claude-family model then emits `outcome` from habit, zod strips it silently with `ok:true`, and the transcript shows the same undifferentiated list twice while the assistant's prose claims it marked items fixed — the tool output contradicts the narration, which is the shape of the `SendUserFile` regression this repo already shipped once. (2) Building any findings surface: the payload cannot distinguish a re-report, so the UI would have to guess, and a well-behaved model will not even send the state because the projected item schema says `additionalProperties: false`.
notes: Every cited file was read in full at the cited lines, and the two behavioural claims were probed rather than inferred: the live projected JSON schema (item-level `additionalProperties: false`) and the silent strip (`safeParse` returns `ok:true` with `outcome` removed) both come from running `getToolDefsAsJsonSchema`/`ReportFindingsSchema` against the repo source, not from reading zod docs. Deliberately OUT of scope, though the challenger noted them: Claude's live tool also carries `line`, `short_summary`, `verdict [CONFIRMED, PLAUSIBLE]` and a top-level `level [low..max]`. None of those is bound by code-review.md — :312 says only "file location", a "one-sentence summary" and a "category tag" — nor by tools-reference.md:45, so they are separate findings, not part of f142; adding them here would be deriving a contract from a tool definition instead of a doc page. Not verified, because it is a judgement for the owner rather than a fact: whether the top-level report should also carry a state (the page marks findings individually, so per-finding is the documented granularity, and that is what this spec proposes). `code-review.md` is row 95 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md`, verdict still `⬜` with no plan, so nothing in the audit contradicts or pre-decides this.
